strings: Prospector Ironband has not heard from Prospector Agmond in weeks. Agmond was in charge of the excavation sites in the Badlands, and Ironband wants Agmond found so the report can be collected.

Agmond ran the excavations in the Badlands, to the southwest. Ironband says "ran" on purpose, for there has been no word from Agmond in weeks. Ironband wants Agmond found, and the report with him. Agmond was last heard of at the farthest-south dig of the Badlands, a small outfit beyond Angor Fortress, and that is where the search should begin.
At the end of the search you find a skeleton, which must be what is left of Agmond. The body is broken and battered, and the bones have been picked clean.
Agmond ran the excavations in the Badlands, southwest of Prospector Ironband.

Why is Prospector Ironband looking for Agmond?
Ironband has not heard from Agmond in weeks and wants to get Agmond's report.

Where was Prospector Agmond last known to be?
At the farthest-south dig of the Badlands, a small outfit beyond Angor Fortress.

Agmond's battered remains lie in the Badlands, and a name is scrawled in the sandstone beside the dead hand: Murdaloc. Agmond's killer is to be put down, with word carried back to Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan.

Agmond's trail comes in from the west, and the blood smeared over stone and sand tells how far the dwarf crawled before dying here. Beside the lifeless hand, scratched into the Badlands sandstone, is a single word: Murdaloc. Agmond's killer is to be slain, along with a number of Stonevault Bonesnappers, and the news taken to Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan.

Ironband takes the news soberly, remembering Agmond as strong of arm, fierce with a hammer and thick of skull. Ironband says Agmond was killed by cursed troggs, and is sure Agmond took a good number of them down along the way.
Agmond was a dwarf in charge of the excavation sites in the Badlands for Prospector Ironband. Your search for Agmond ended at a skeleton.
Murdaloc is the name scrawled in the sandstone beside Agmond's dead hand. You are to slay Agmond's killer, Murdaloc.
Where does the report need to go?
To Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan.

This step in the investigation leads deep into an old crate of Flintridge heirlooms left beside the canals of Stormwind City. Sifting through the dusty relics uncovers a torn journal page, offering a vital handwritten clue to the past life of Stalvan Mistmantle that leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest.

While digging through a sealed crate filled with musty heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits, investigators uncover a lone torn journal page hidden beneath a ceramic vase. Written in Stalvan Mistmantle's own hand, this remnant provides an intimate glimpse into the mind of a reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

Marshal Haggard, now aged and plagued by failing eyesight, struggles to read the script on the battered parchment. Even so, the distinctive handwriting strikes an uneasy chord in his memory, recalling documents and incidents from years past before the darkness took his sight.
Where is the sealed crate located?

The sealed crate sits by the Canals of Stormwind City, directly behind Caretaker Folsom among the Flintridge family's packed-up belongings. The page you find there is then taken to Marshal Haggard in southeastern Elwynn Forest.
crate location | where is crate | haggard crate
What is inside the sealed crate?
The crate contains dusty heirlooms, a family portrait, old books, hunting trophies, and a ceramic vase, beneath which lies a torn page from Stalvan's journal.
crate contents | what is in the crate | torn page crate

Marshal Haggard is an elderly, retired officer of Stormwind living alone in southern Elwynn Forest. Despite his failing eyesight and frailty, his memories of old records and travelers make him a crucial witness to past events.
who is haggard | marshal haggard lore | old marshal elwynn
Why is this journal page important?

The torn journal page is direct evidence written by Stalvan Mistmantle himself. Its distinctive penmanship and lingering thoughts help tie disparate accounts across Duskwood and Elwynn back to his personal downfall.
why torn page matters | journal page clue | stalvan journal
What happens when the crate is opened?
Disturbing the remnants of Stalvan's past stirs the restless dead, causing a vengeful Forlorn Spirit to manifest and strike at those trying to unravel the tragedy.

Where does the investigation lead next?
After presenting the torn page to Marshal Haggard, his recollection of the handwriting guides the investigation onward to find more surviving fragments of Stalvan's history.

Investigating old cold cases in the heart of Elwynn reveals how deeply personal horrors can slip past the eyes of Stormwind's marshals.
Marshal Haggard represents the aging veteran generation of Stormwind, holding vital memories of the kingdom before the First and Second Wars tore families apart.
Hollee sends Remtravel's fossil from Darkshore to Darnassus. She stays behind to watch the wandering prospector, and Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker takes a keen interest in the find.

Prospector Remtravel has unearthed a curious fossil along Darkshore's coast. He cares more about digging deeper than following protocol. Archaeologist Hollee stays behind to watch over him among the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists. She asks you, an Alliance traveler, to carry the specimen to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild keeps a scholarly delegation.

Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea under the Explorers' League banner, searching Kalimdor's soil for ancient relics and lost history. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker marvels at Remtravel's knack for finding ancient treasures. Night elves see their forests as living sanctuaries, while the League sees ancient lands as ground to study and decipher.
Prospector Remtravel unearthed an unidentified petrified specimen along Darkshore's coast. Its age and strange nature make it a prized find for the Explorers' League scholars in Darnassus.

King Magni Bronzebeard chartered the Explorers' League to uncover the origins of the dwarven race and ancient history across Azeroth. Friendly ties with the night elves let dwarven scholars base expeditions in Darnassus and study Kalimdor's forgotten lands.

As a dwarf, carrying Remtravel's fossil serves the Explorers' League's chief aim: uncovering the world's deep past and showing the worth of dwarven perseverance.
As a night elf, seeing dwarven excavators bring ancient remnants from Darkshore's sacred soil can be jarring. Cooperation with the League preserves Alliance bonds.

Hollee is determined not to abandon Darkshore while Remtravel remains behind in the wilderness, so she relies on you to ferry the priceless find directly to Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker in Darnassus on their behalf.

In Thunder Bluff, the Ashenvale Hunt calls young Horde champions north to serve at the forest outposts. Heralds direct them to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post for a proving hunt.
A Summons from the High Rise

Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation through Thunder Bluff for proven adventurers. The Horde has established footholds in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, and its outposts need young warriors. Those who answer will face a harsher land and test their survival skills beyond Mulgore.

Ashenvale offers the Horde rich resources and severe peril. Splintertree Post stands along the main road, while a remote outpost lies on the western coast at Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman, organizes a great hunt to tame the wilderness and win glory for the Horde.
Who offers this quest in Thunder Bluff?
Bluff Runner Windstrider offers the summons to passing adventurers in Thunder Bluff. He alerts capable fighters to the Horde's efforts to expand and points them toward outposts that need aid.
who starts ashenvale hunt | quest giver ashenvale hunt | bluff runner windstrider

As Horde, you rely on Splintertree Post and Zoram Strand to support the northern supply lines. Fresh recruits help keep wild beasts and hostile natives at bay.

Ruul Eagletalon asks you to test your readiness against the Windfury harpies in Mulgore. The hunt takes you to the southeastern cliffs, where their speed and claws put your skill to the test before you leave the tauren homeland.

In Bloodhoof Village, Ruul Eagletalon watches travelers pass through Mulgore. He asks those coming of age or preparing for wider travels to prove their combat instincts. Beyond Mulgore's sheltered valleys, survival demands poise against cunning foes, and Ruul measures your mettle against the land's fiercest native predators.

The Windfury harpies roost along Mulgore's southeastern mountain rim, away from the beaten trails. They threaten wandering wildlife and isolated travelers, diving swiftly and striking with razor-sharp claws as they hunt for fresh flesh. Defeating them and bringing back their talons proves you can overcome a settled threat and react quickly to aerial attackers.
Ruul Eagletalon is a veteran tauren warrior and teacher in Bloodhoof Village. He tests young adventurers before they travel into the more perilous reaches of Kalimdor.

Preparation for Ceremony is a tauren tradition focused on crafting a ceremonial headdress for one preparing to appear before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof. To finish the traditional attire, vibrant feathers must be collected from dangerous harpies nesting beyond Thunder Bluff while the leather bands are prepared.

In tauren culture, standing before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof is an occasion of great pride and reverence. Such milestones demand proper ceremonial attire, particularly a traditional headdress carefully fashioned from treated leather and symbolic plumage. Crafting this regalia is considered an honor by family members, who take great care to ensure every component reflects dignity and respect before the leader of the united tribes.

Constructing a ceremonial headdress requires both skill and specific materials. While supple leather straps are tanned to form the base band, long and pristine feathers must be sourced to adorn the crown. The avian harpies roosting across the craggy hills to the north and northwest of Thunder Bluff provide feathers of the exact size and coloration required, calling upon travelers to venture into hostile nests to retrieve them.
What ceremony is being prepared for?

The ceremony marks a tauren presenting himself before Chief Cairne Bloodhoof. To mark this honorable occasion, his sibling is crafting a special ceremonial headdress fashioned from tanned leather and vibrant feathers.

Chief Cairne Bloodhoof is the venerable high chieftain and leader of the united tauren tribes, ruling from the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. Standing before him is a distinct honor for any tauren.

Aiding a fellow member of the Horde in their traditional ceremonial duties honors the customs of the tauren allies atop the mesas of Thunder Bluff.

Headdresses crafted from natural materials are deeply tied to tauren honor and rites of passage before the high chieftain. Helping fashion such regalia reflects the communal spirit and pride of the tribes of Mulgore.

In Mulgore, Baine Bloodhoof calls you to stop Palemane gnolls from killing the plains' wildlife. By striking their hunters, you help protect the herds and the tauren way of living with the Earth Mother.

The tauren take from the land only what they need and honor the Earth Mother in all things. Palemane gnolls have settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, where they slaughter wildlife across the plains. Their hunting leaves carcasses behind and harms the balance of the grasslands. The tauren are building a peaceful home in Mulgore, but the gnolls' wasteful killing threatens it.

Baine Bloodhoof tried to speak with the Palemane gnolls and settle the matter peacefully. They rejected every attempt and kept killing wildlife. Now Baine sends young braves to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer lasting harm.
The Circle of Life and Death
When you return, Baine teaches that taking life is never for malice, but may be needed to keep harmony. Life and death form a circle, and every guardian of Mulgore must carry that truth.
Baine Bloodhoof, son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, gives you this work in Bloodhoof Village, in central Mulgore.

The Palemane gnolls hunt Mulgore's wildlife recklessly and deplete the herds. They also rejected the tauren's attempts to speak peacefully.

At Bloodhoof Village, Baine Bloodhoof fears the dwarves' digging will anger Mulgore's beasts and scar its sacred earth. He asks young Horde defenders to break the prospectors' picks and halt their work.

Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have marked out a dig site in Mulgore's hills. The Explorer's League searches Kalimdor for titan relics and secrets of the earthen, often without regard for the lands or customs of those who live there. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother, worthy of reverence rather than excavation for stone and metal.

Baine Bloodhoof sees the dwarves' machines and blasting as a threat to the plains' fragile balance. Their noise agitates the local wildlife and stirs the kodos into frenzy. The tauren mean to smash the prospectors' picks at the forges, sending a blunt warning and stopping the digging before it causes lasting harm.

Grull Hawkwind judges the newcomers who hope to leave Red Cloud Mesa for the wider plains of Mulgore. Before they can meet his father, Chief Hawkwind, he asks them to prove their ability. A successful hunt shows self-reliance and helps support the tribe.
